Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

replace verb

put a new one in place of

also substitute, replacement, put a new one in

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.5.72 (Lewis & Short): in eōrum locum cīvēs Rōmānōs
Traupman 185, 387

substituō, substituere, substituī, substitūtum

verb, third conjugation; with in locum and the genitive

put in place of, substitute

Lewis & Short: “to put instead or in the place of another, to substitute (class.)”.

Other words

  • repōnō, repōnere, reposuī, repositum — replace (what was lost or broken); put back

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Tac. Ann. 1.63 (Lewis & Short): ruptōs vetustāte pontēs; Verg. A. 5.752 (Lewis & Short): flammīs ambēsa repōnunt rōbora nāvigiīs

    Lewis & Short: “to replace, restore”. For putting a thing back where it was, see put away.

Examples

  • Hoc frāctum est; aliud in ejus locum substituam.

    This one’s broken; I’ll replace it.composed

See also replace, put away, repair.

SourcesLewis & Short: substituo · Lewis & Short: repono

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 185, 387, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
